newsitem.title: USA: NYSE lifts curbs as Dow Industrials slash gains.
newsitem.headline: NYSE lifts curbs as Dow Industrials slash gains.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange lifted its curbs on index-arbitrage trades at 0959 EST/1459 GMT as profit-taking and a weak bond market led the Dow to slash its earlier gains.
The Industrials were up 18 points at 6323 after having run as high as 6356 after the opening bell. Advances narrowed their lead over declining issues to 10 to eight.
"It would appear to me as though the problem is in the bond market," said Hugh Johsnon, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.

"It's not entirely unrelated to strong numbers we saw this morning, but there is a report of a substantial seller in the credit markets who has show up in the last five to 10 minutes. This is creating softness in bonds and stocks."
The early rally was due in large part to excitement generated by a $13 billion merger deal between McDonnell Douglas Corp and Boeing Co.
The long bond was down 13/32 to yield 6.61 percent.
